questions.q: Which switching technology characterises the second generation of computers?
questions.model: Second-generation computers replaced vacuum tubes with transistors.

questions.t: bit, byte, KB, MB, GB and their relations to each other
questions.q: A file occupies 3 MB. Using binary prefixes (1 KB = 1024 bytes, 1 MB = 1024 KB), how many bytes does it occupy?
Explain the computer system memory hierarchy from registers to secondary storage, and state how access time, cost per bit and capacity change as one moves down the hierarchy.
questions.model: Registers, cache, main memory (RAM), secondary storage (disk/SSD). Moving down: access time increases, cost per bit decreases, capacity increases. Faster, costlier memory is kept small and close to the CPU.

questions.q: Write an algorithm and draw the corresponding flowchart that reads a positive integer N and prints the sum of its digits. Use a loop and show the decision symbol that terminates it.
questions.model: Algorithm: read N; sum = 0; while N > 0: sum = sum + N mod 10, N = N div 10; print sum. Flowchart: start, input N, initialise sum, decision 'N > 0?' (yes: update sum and N, loop back; no: output sum), stop.

questions.t: How to read and print on screen
questions.q: In C, the standard library function ___ reads formatted input from the keyboard, and ___ writes a single character to the screen.
questions.model: scanf() reads formatted input; putchar() writes one character.

questions.q: Describe the stages in the life of a C program from source file to execution, naming the output of each stage.
questions.model: Preprocessing (expanded source, .i), compilation (assembly, .s), assembly (object code, .o), linking (executable), loading (program placed in memory), execution.

questions.q: True or False: In C, 'extern int count;' is a declaration that does not allocate storage for count, whereas 'int count = 0;' at file scope is a definition.
questions.model: True. A declaration introduces the name and type; a definition also allocates storage.

questions.q: Using C operator precedence and associativity, what value does x hold after: int x = 10 - 4 / 2 * 3 + 7 % 3;
Read the assertion and reason about bitwise operators and choose the correct option.
questions.assertion: For an unsigned int x, the expression x & 1 is 1 exactly when x is odd.
questions.reason: The least significant bit of a binary number is 1 for odd numbers and 0 for even numbers.
questions.model: Both are true and R explains A: masking with 1 isolates the least significant bit.

questions.q: Write a C program that reads three integers and prints the largest of them using nested if-else statements.

A menu-driven program dispatches on an integer choice from 1 to 6. Compare an if-else ladder and a switch statement for this task in terms of readability and execution performance, and state which you would choose.
questions.model: switch on a small dense integer range compiles to a jump table (constant time) and reads as a list of cases; an if-else ladder evaluates conditions in sequence. switch is preferred; if-else suits ranges and non-integer conditions.

questions.q: Which C loop executes its body at least once even when its condition is false at the start?
questions.model: do while is exit-controlled: the condition is tested after the body.

questions.q: What is printed by: int s = 0; for (int i = 1; i <= 10; i++) { if (i % 3 == 0) continue; if (i > 8) break; s += i; } printf("%d", s);
questions.model: Adds 1,2,4,5,7,8 (3 and 6 skipped, loop breaks at 9): 1+2+4+5+7+8 = 27.

questions.q: Write recursive and iterative C functions to compute n! and use the function call stack to compare them for memory use and speed. Recommend one for n up to 20 and justify your choice.
questions.model: Recursive: return n <= 1 ? 1 : n * fact(n - 1); iterative loop multiplies 2..n. Recursion uses one stack frame per call (O(n) stack) and call overhead; iteration uses O(1) extra space. Use the iterative version (and unsigned long long, since 20! fits in 64 bits).

questions.q: A local variable must keep its value between successive calls of a function. Which storage class should it have?
questions.model: A static local variable has static lifetime but block scope, so it keeps its value between calls.

questions.q: A student writes void swap(int a, int b) { int t = a; a = b; b = t; } and calls swap(x, y), but x and y are unchanged. Explain why, using the call-by-value mechanism.
questions.model: C passes copies of the arguments; swap exchanges its local copies a and b, which are destroyed on return, so x and y in the caller are unchanged. Pointers would be needed to modify the caller's variables.

questions.t: computing address of an element in array
questions.q: An int array A[50] starts at base address 2000 and sizeof(int) is 4 bytes. What is the address of A[17]?
questions.model: Address = base + index x size = 2000 + 17 x 4 = 2068.

questions.q: Write a C function int linear_search(int a[], int n, int key) that returns the index of key in a, or -1 if it is absent, and show a call from main for an array of 8 elements.
True or False: The C compiler checks array bounds at run time and stops the program when an index such as a[10] is used on int a[10].
questions.model: False. C performs no bound checking; out-of-bounds access is undefined behaviour and may cause a segmentation fault.

questions.q: Design a C program for the case: read the marks, store them in an array, and print the class average, the highest mark and how many students scored above the average.
questions.case: A teacher records the marks (0 to 100) of 30 students in a test and needs a short report: the class average, the highest mark, and the number of students who scored above the average.
questions.model: Declare int marks[30]; read with a loop; compute sum and max in one pass; average = sum / 30.0; second pass counts marks[i] > average; print the three results. Validate input range 0-100.
